purpose: confirm with the right people that the written requirements are correct, complete, consistent and testable before design and build rely on them
entry_criteria: Stakeholders and a product owner are available
Acceptance criteria exist for the requirements
procedure: Check each requirement against the quality attributes: necessary, unambiguous, testable, consistent, feasible and traceable to a need.
Check the set for gaps against the process models and the goals, and for conflicts between requirements and with the rules.
Walk the stakeholders through scenarios built from the requirements, and record where the scenario does not match their expectations.
Review with developers and testers: can it be built and can each criterion be tested.
Log each finding with the requirement id, the problem and the decision, and update the requirements.
Have the product owner approve the validated baseline in writing and set the change process from then on.
acceptance_criteria: Every requirement was checked against the named attributes
Gaps and conflicts are logged with decisions
The product owner approved the baseline
validation_method: Product owner approval of the baseline.

validation.check: check every requirement id has a source need, an acceptance criterion and a review result
trace three goals to the requirements that satisfy them

failure_modes.response: Resolve with the owner and record

failure_modes.detection: Tester cannot judge pass or fail

worked_example: ILLUSTRATIVE: A walkthrough of the refund scenario shows two requirements give different time limits. The owner decides on 30 days, both are corrected, and the baseline is approved with the finding logged.
